cargo 1.94.1 (29ea6fb6a 2026-03-24)

# How each fixture in this directory was produced
#
# The hand-written fixtures are compiled standalone from the source file that
# sits next to them, from *this directory*, so that the `<impl at FILE:l:c>`
# headers and `{closure@FILE:l:c: l:c}` spans name the checked-in `.rs` file:
#
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir -o spike.mir              spike.rs
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir -o format_and_outparams.mir format_and_outparams.rs
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir -o async_multi_await.mir  async_multi_await.rs
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir -o generic_layers.mir     generic_layers.rs
#
# The two fixtures added for the adversarial-review gaps were produced the same
# way but on **rustc 1.98.0 (88d9e12ae 2026-08-18)**, the toolchain CI runs, so
# the suite exercises both ends of the validated 1.94-1.98 range rather than
# only the older one:
#
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir \
#         -o implicit_and_higher_order.mir implicit_and_higher_order.rs
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir -o parse_drift.mir parse_drift.rs
#
# The three fixtures added for review round 2 were produced on rustc 1.98.0
# (88d9e12ae 2026-08-18) as well, from this directory:
#
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir -o shadowed_statics.mir shadowed_statics.rs
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir -o shadowed_impls.mir   shadowed_impls.rs
#
# The two fixtures added for review round 4 were produced on rustc 1.98.0
# (88d9e12ae 2026-08-18) as well, from this directory:
#
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir -o shadowed_closures.mir shadowed_closures.rs
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir -o shadowed_drops.mir    shadowed_drops.rs
#
# `shadowed_closures.mir` is checked for the property it exists to pin: two
# DIFFERENT bodies must print the SAME `{closure@shadowed_closures.rs:L:C}`,
# because the closure is written inside a `macro_rules!` body and so carries the
# macro definition's span. If a future rustc ever gives each expansion its own
# span, re-emit it and update the span string in
# `resolve_fixtures::a_closure_span_two_bodies_share_resolves_to_the_enclosing_ones`
# — and if the collision is gone entirely, say so there rather than deleting the
# test, since the resolver still has to handle dumps from the toolchains that do
# collide. Check with
#
#   grep -o '{closure@[^}]*}' shadowed_closures.mir | sort | uniq -c
#
# `bodyless_dependency.mir` needs TWO steps, because its point is a callee whose
# body the analysis never sees. The stub crate is compiled to an rlib WITHOUT
# `--emit=mir`, exactly as a dependency outside a `--package` scope is:
#
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --crate-name bodyless_dep_stub \
#         -o libbodyless_dep_stub.rlib bodyless_dep_stub.rs
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir \
#         --extern bodyless_dep_stub=libbodyless_dep_stub.rlib \
#         -o bodyless_dependency.mir bodyless_dependency.rs
#   rm libbodyless_dep_stub.rlib
#
# The rlib is a build artifact and is deliberately NOT checked in; only
# `bodyless_dep_stub.rs` and the emitted `.mir` are. rustc trims the callee to a
# bare `now_ish()` in the dump, which is the whole point of the fixture.
#
# `trait_path_trust.mir` (review round 5) needs the same TWO steps, and for the
# same reason: the impl whose trust is at stake must have no body in the
# analyzed set. From this directory:
#
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --crate-name trait_path_dep_stub \
#         -o libtrait_path_dep_stub.rlib trait_path_dep_stub.rs
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir \
#         --extern trait_path_dep_stub=libtrait_path_dep_stub.rlib \
#         -o trait_path_trust.mir trait_path_trust.rs
#   rm libtrait_path_dep_stub.rlib
#
# The property it pins is a PRINTING one, so check it after re-emitting: the
# dump must still spell the trait out and leave the self type a dependency's.
#
#   grep -n 'convert::Into\|convert::From' trait_path_trust.mir
#
# must show `<Clock as std::convert::Into<std::string::String>>::into` (the
# finding: std in the trait only) and
# `<std::string::String as std::convert::From<&str>>::from` (the control: std in
# the self type). The full spelling comes from the fixture's `shadow` module,
# whose `String`, `Into` and `From` names stop rustc trimming those paths; if a
# future rustc trims them anyway, re-shape the shadow until the two forms above
# appear rather than weakening the test.
#
# `parse_drift_garbled.mir` is NOT compiled: it is a byte-for-byte copy of
# `parse_drift.mir` with exactly one call terminator rewritten from
# `_4 = wall_clock_secs() -> [..]` to `_4 <== wall_clock_secs() -> [..]`,
# simulating a future rustc that prints a call differently. Regenerate it with
#
#   sed '136s/_4 = wall_clock_secs()/_4 <== wall_clock_secs()/' \
#       parse_drift.mir > parse_drift_garbled.mir
#
# after re-emitting `parse_drift.mir`, checking that line 136 is still the
# `wall_clock_secs` call. The point of the fixture is that the mutated dump must
# come back `unknown: mir-parse`, never `proven-deterministic`.
#
# `example_deterministic_primitives.mir` is a real, untrimmed dump of a real
# workspace example (do not trim it: the bodies are interdependent). From the
# workspace root:
#
#   cargo rustc -p autumn-harvest --example deterministic_primitives \
#       --no-default-features --features testing \
#       --target-dir target/agent-engine -- --emit=mir -C opt-level=0
#
# and the result was copied from
#
#   target/agent-engine/debug/examples/deterministic_primitives-e38e618daf843f63.mir
#
# Its `<impl at ...>` headers are relative to the WORKSPACE ROOT
# (`autumn-harvest/examples/deterministic_primitives.rs`), not to this
# directory, so resolution tests must use the workspace root as a source root.

# `saga_graph/flow.mir` (issue #2010) was produced on rustc 1.99.0
# (b940084d7 2026-09-28), the toolchain `rust-toolchain.toml` pins. It needs
# TWO steps, like `bodyless_dependency.mir`: the stub `autumn_harvest` crate
# must have no body in the analyzed set, and its crate name makes it trusted.
# From `saga_graph/`:
#
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --crate-name autumn_harvest \
#         -o libautumn_harvest.rlib harvest_stub.rs
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir \
#         --extern autumn_harvest=libautumn_harvest.rlib -o flow.mir flow.rs
#   rm libautumn_harvest.rlib
#
# The flow graph reads the `?` lowering: `Try::branch`, a `switchInt` with
# cases `0` and `1`, and `from_residual`. After a re-emit, check that each
# `saga.step(..).await?` still prints that shape:
#
#   grep -c 'as Try>::branch' saga_graph/flow.mir
#
# Expect 28, one per `?` in `saga_graph/flow.rs`. The walk also hard-codes
# the case values: `0` is `Poll::Ready` and `ControlFlow::Continue`, and `1`
# is `ControlFlow::Break`. A change to them is not detected by the count, so
# run `cargo test -p autumn-harvest-verify --test saga_graph` after a re-emit.
#
# `async_block_follow/flow.mir` (issue #2010) was produced the same way, on
# rustc 1.99.0, with a second stub crate that stands for an untrusted
# dependency. From `async_block_follow/`:
#
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --crate-name autumn_harvest \
#         -o libautumn_harvest.rlib harvest_stub.rs
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --crate-name other_crate \
#         -o libother_crate.rlib other_crate.rs
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir \
#         --extern autumn_harvest=libautumn_harvest.rlib \
#         --extern other_crate=libother_crate.rlib -o flow.mir flow.rs
#   rm libautumn_harvest.rlib libother_crate.rlib

# `saga_graph_own/flow.mir` (issue #2010) holds a workflow crate's own type
# named `Saga`. It uses the stub of `saga_graph/` and the same two steps,
# from `saga_graph_own/`:
#
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --crate-name autumn_harvest \
#         -o libautumn_harvest.rlib harvest_stub.rs
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir \
#         --extern autumn_harvest=libautumn_harvest.rlib -o flow.mir flow.rs
#   rm libautumn_harvest.rlib
#
# It is a fixture of its own on purpose. In one dump with the engine's
# `Saga`, the resolver maps the trimmed `Saga::<'_>::new` to the local impl
# by name. That adds a conservative `external-const` boundary, not a wrong
# verdict, and it is outside the scope of issue #2010. The type has a field
# for a like reason: MIR prints a unit struct value as `const own::Saga`, and
# the structure digest reads that as an `external-const` boundary.

# `saga_graph_renamed/flow.mir` (issue #2010) reaches the engine through a
# renamed crate and through a facade crate. MIR prints the defining crate,
# `autumn_harvest::Saga`, for both. From `saga_graph_renamed/`:
#
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --crate-name autumn_harvest \
#         -o libautumn_harvest.rlib ../saga_graph/harvest_stub.rs
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --crate-name facade \
#         --extern autumn_harvest=libautumn_harvest.rlib \
#         -o libfacade.rlib facade.rs
#   rustc --crate-type lib --edition 2024 --emit=mir \
#         --extern ah=libautumn_harvest.rlib \
#         --extern facade=libfacade.rlib -L . -o flow.mir flow.rs
#   rm libautumn_harvest.rlib libfacade.rlib
